Cruz squeezes his nose to feel cartilage, works the grabber arm to pick up the Megalodon tooth, and shouts \"A hammerhead!\" Phoenix notices \"There aren't any trees,\" names the \"nightlight shark,\" and makes the Tooth Fairy joke. Neither child is ever silent. No likes or notes were in the brief, so none could shape a scene.","craft":"The story opens in the bedroom with Phoenix's LEGO shark world. The brick clicks and builds a submarine. Every chapter has a hands-on beat or discovery (nose squeeze, grabber arm, walking shark, curious great white). It returns home with a tooth keepsake and the callback \"Older than dinosaurs\" / \"Older than TREES.\" The whole has a clear time-travel shape from ancient to today.","facts":"Most facts are correct and woven into action (cartilage via the nose squeeze, over 500 species, epaulette walking, tooth conveyor belt). Two small problems. \"They can smell a tiny drop of blood from very far away\" repeats a popular exaggeration without hedging. Helicoprion is presented as a shark, but it was a shark-like relative of ratfish. The True Facts list also shifts the tooth from \"bigger than Cruz's whole hand\" to \"bigger than a grown-up's hand.\"","age_fit":"The prose is short and repetitive, with sound words (SPLOOSH, WHOOOOSH), and cartilage and plankton are explained in-story. There is some tension for Band A, where the peril level is none: \"Why is everybody hiding?\" as Megalodon's shadow passes, and \"Rows and rows of teeth!\" with Phoenix holding Cruz's hand. Both resolve at once. At 1851 words the story is over the 1300-1700 target but inside the 15% tolerance.","continuity":"The opening refers back to the LEGO adventure a week earlier. The red brick glows and clicks to start the adventure and glows again to send them home. WHOOOOSH is used throughout, and \"Play well\" becomes a fitting \"Swim well.\" The story adds one strong new recurring character, Grandpa Greenie, and sets up his return.","delight":"There are jokes that land for parent and child alike: \"The Tooth Fairy must be SO busy,\" \"Yuck!\" said Phoenix, delighted, and Greenland sharks \"do everything slowly, including thinking.\" The weak spot is the conservation passage in Chapter 6. It turns into a paragraph-long sermon (\"getting serious\") that slows the read-aloud rhythm."},"caps_applied":["none"],"disqualified":false,"overall":4.5,"editor_notes":["Turn the Chapter 6 conservation speech into something the boys do or say. Hedge or replace the \"drop of blood from very far away\" line, which is both a popular exaggeration and an odd image at bedtime.","Trim about 150 words to bring the story closer to the 1700 target, for instance by tightening the Chapter 1 submarine build. It bent and wiggled.","worst_moment":"Lots of sharks are in danger because of people fishing too many of them. Sharks help keep the whole ocean healthy."}
